index.title: Pixel Home: cozy queue-sorting puzzles
index.description: Pixel Home is a cozy pixel-art puzzle about getting everyone home. 300 gardens in twenty worlds, a fresh daily puzzle and no timers.
index.tagline: Sort the colors, mind the queue and get every pip home. A cozy pixel-art puzzle for iPhone and iPad.
index.shotTitle: The Pixel Home title screen with lives, the shop, gifts and postcards
index.shotBrookside: A Brookside garden: two homes, their orders and the Flow Line
index.shotGlowcave: A Glowcave garden with a color gate
index.shotPostcards: Pixel Postcards revealed one piece per cleared level
index.shotGifts: The daily gift and three daily missions
index.clip: Scan the code with your iPhone camera to open the Pixel Home App Clip: today's Daily Flow in seconds, with nothing to install. If you like it, the full game is one tap away.
index.clipQrAlt: QR code that opens the Pixel Home App Clip
index.how1: Little critters called pips wait in their burrows. Tap one to send it out. If its home is ready, it walks straight there. If not, it waits in the Flow Line, and the line moves strictly first in, first out.
index.how2: Homes take one color at a time and the line is short, so the order you choose is the whole puzzle. Plan it, keep the line moving and fill every home.
index.worlds: From the Meadow to Prism Falls, new ideas arrive gently: switches that redirect the path, Nooks where a pip can rest, color gates, and a Stretch that lends you one more slot. Clear one of the first ten worlds and it opens again by moonlight, with harder gardens on paths you know.
index.daily: The Daily Flow is a new garden each day, the same for every player, with its own Game Center leaderboard.
index.pace: No level timers. Undo, hints and rewinding to the last solvable moment are always free.
index.lives: A life is used only when you give up a jammed attempt at a new level. Replays, Challenge runs and the Daily Flow never cost one.
index.collect: Up to three stars per garden, Pixel Postcards revealed piece by piece, a daily gift, daily missions and new garden looks.
index.devices: Optional Sign in with Apple keeps your garden in your own iCloud. Game Center is there if you want it. Playing as a guest is complete.
index.free1: Pixel Home is free to play. Optional in-app purchases offer extra lives, 24 hours of unlimited lives and Stretch boosters; the daily gift, missions and awards give the same things for free. From version 1.1 the game is supported by ads that never interrupt a level: a short one after every fifth garden you clear, and a video you can choose to watch for an extra life.
index.free2: We collect no data that identifies you, and the ads are never personalized. Read the privacy policy, or visit support if you need a hand.

support.title: Pixel Home support
support.description: Help with Pixel Home: lives, purchases, saving progress, Game Center and how to get in touch.
support.heading: Support
support.lead: Answers to the common questions, and how to reach us.
support.contact: Tell us what happened, which device and iOS version you use, and the version shown at the bottom of the game's Settings.
support.lives: You have five lives, and one comes back every 30 minutes. A life is used only when an attempt at a level you haven't cleared jams and you then restart or leave it. Undo, hints, rewind, replays of cleared levels, Challenge runs and the Daily Flow never cost a life.
support.ads: From version 1.1, a short ad appears after every fifth level you clear, never during one. When you are out of lives you can also choose to watch a video for one, up to three a day. No ad is shown between levels while unlimited lives are running. If you were asked for your consent, you can change your answer under Settings, then Ad choices.
support.stuck: Use Hint for the next useful move. If the flow jams, Rewind takes you back to the last position that can still be solved. Both are free and unlimited.
support.purchase1: Close and reopen the game. A purchase that was interrupted is delivered when the game starts.
support.purchase2: Open the shop and tap Restore purchases. Life packs, unlimited lives and boosters are used up when bought, so there is nothing to restore later, but this collects anything still waiting.
support.purchase3: With Ask to Buy, the items arrive once the purchase is approved.
support.purchase4: For refunds, use reportaproblem.apple.com. Purchases are handled by Apple.
support.progressTitle: Keeping progress on a new device
support.progress1: Open your profile (the gardener badge on the title screen) and choose Sign in with Apple. Your progress is then saved to your own iCloud and follows you to any iPhone or iPad signed in to the same Apple Account with iCloud turned on. Syncing can take up to a minute.
support.progress2: The five regenerating lives belong to each device. Bought and earned lives travel with your save.
support.gameCenter: Game Center is optional. Nothing happens until you tap Sign in to Game Center in your profile. If that says to sign in in the Settings app, open Settings, then Game Center, and sign in there first.
support.delete: In your profile, Delete account data removes the cloud save linked to your Apple Account and signs you out. Deleting the app removes your progress and settings from the device. Your lives and what your purchases granted are kept in the iOS Keychain, so they are still there if you install the game again. To stop using Sign in with Apple with Pixel Home, open the Settings app, tap your name, then Sign in with Apple.

privacy.title: Pixel Home privacy policy
privacy.description: What Pixel Home does with data. From version 1.1 the game shows ads delivered by Google, never personalized. From version 1.2 it sends anonymous play statistics that you can turn off.
privacy.heading: Privacy policy
privacy.summary: We do not collect any data that identifies you. Pixel Home has no accounts on our side and no tracking, and we run no servers for it. From version 1.1 the game shows ads. They are delivered by Google, which receives some information from your device to do that; the sections on advertising below say what, when, and what you can choose. From version 1.2 the game also sends anonymous play statistics, which you can turn off; the section on them says what they contain.
privacy.device: Your progress and settings are stored on your device. Your lives, the record of what your purchases granted and your sign-in are kept in the iOS Keychain on your device, where they can remain after the game is deleted, so that they are still there if you install it again. None of this is sent to us.
privacy.signIn: You can play as a guest. If you choose to sign in, the game asks Apple only for your name, never your email address. Apple gives the game an identifier for your account. It is kept on your device and used to label your save in your own iCloud storage. We have no server, so neither the identifier nor your name ever reaches us.
privacy.icloud: When you are signed in, your progress is saved to your own iCloud key-value storage so it can follow you to your other devices. That storage belongs to your Apple Account. We cannot read it. Apple's handling of it is covered by Apple's privacy policy.
privacy.gameCenter: If you choose to sign in to Game Center, your scores and achievements are sent to Apple's Game Center under your Game Center profile. The game does not start Game Center until you ask for it.
privacy.purchases: In-app purchases are processed by Apple. We never see your payment details.
privacy.ads: From version 1.1, Pixel Home shows two kinds of ad, both delivered by Google AdMob: a full-screen ad after every fifth level you clear, and a video you can choose to watch for an extra life. Ads never appear during a level. Version 1.0 shows no ads and contains no advertising software. Nothing is sent to Google until an ad is first needed: when you ask for a video, or shortly before the first ad between levels.
privacy.adsData: To deliver ads, limit how often they appear and measure them, Google's advertising software in the game sends Google information such as your IP address (which shows roughly where you are), details of your device and the app (model, system version, language, app version), identifiers kept for the app on your device, and whether an ad was shown or tapped. This information goes to Google and its advertising partners, not to us. How Google uses information from apps that use its services explains what Google does with it and how you can control it.
privacy.adsChoiceTitle: No personalized ads, and your choices
privacy.adsChoice: The game always asks for non-personalized ads. It never asks for permission to track you across other companies' apps and websites, so your advertising identifier is not used. Ads may still be chosen from general context, such as roughly where you are, your language and the app you are using. If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, Google's consent form asks for your choice before the first ad and lists the advertising partners involved. You can refuse, and you can change your answer at any time in the game under Settings, then Ad choices.
privacy.stats: From version 1.2, Pixel Home sends anonymous play statistics to PostHog, an analytics service: which levels are started, cleared or given up, when lives run out, when the shop is opened and how purchases end, with the app version and the game's language. They contain no name, account, advertising or device identifier, and nothing that identifies you: a random value that changes every day lets us count players per day without recognizing anyone from one day to the next. They are stored in the European Union, without IP addresses or location. You can turn them off in the game under Settings, then Share anonymous play statistics. How PostHog handles them is covered by PostHog's privacy policy.
privacy.children: We collect no data that identifies anyone, including children: the play statistics are anonymous. Ads are never personalized and are limited to those Google rates as suitable for general audiences.
privacy.site: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages. It uses no cookies and no analytics of its own. GitHub may log technical information such as IP addresses to operate the service, as described in the GitHub privacy statement. From version 1.1 the game also reads a small settings file from this site when it starts, so that it can show fewer ads or say that a new version is available. The request contains nothing about you, but as with any visit GitHub may log the IP address it comes from.
privacy.changes: If this policy changes, the new version will be published on this page with a new effective date.
privacy.language: This policy is published in several languages for convenience. If the versions differ, the English version applies.
privacy.contact: Questions about this policy can be sent to {email}.
